scope: Exact symmetry and normalization price of K1366's repository-owned mu Q-squared regularizer; not a source-derived maximal-compact selector, hypercharge normalization or observed assignment.

symmetry_classification.invariance_group: The regularizer is invariant exactly under unitaries U preserving D(Q) and satisfying U*Q^2U=Q^2; this is the Q-squared commutant/normalizer and contains the selected circle and any charge-sign reversal.
symmetry_classification.full_G_test: If Q^2 commuted with the full irreducible principal-series G action, every spectral projection of Q^2 would lie in the representation commutant and Schur irreducibility would force Q^2 to be scalar.
symmetry_classification.contradiction: K1358 supplies unbounded charges plus_or_minus 4n and a neutral sector, so Q^2 is non-scalar and unbounded; full-G invariance is impossible.
symmetry_classification.symmetry_price: The term makes the compact reduction dynamically operative only after Q is chosen; it preserves the Q-squared commutant, not the full split group.

normalization_classification.rescaling_degeneracy: For every c nonzero, (Q,mu) maps to (cQ,mu/c^2) without changing mu Q^2 or the regularized free operator.
normalization_classification.sign_degeneracy: Q and -Q give the same regularizer and free spectrum.
normalization_classification.selection_limit: The action term presupposes a charge ray and coefficient product; it does not select the primitive generator, orientation, normalization or observed charge labels.
normalization_classification.source_limit: SC-META-53 remains UNCERTAIN and supplies no action coefficient or observed-carrier intertwiner fixing these choices.

claim_ceiling: The positive regularizer has an exact symmetry price: it preserves the Q-squared commutant and cannot be invariant under the full irreducible split-G action. The product mu Q^2 is blind to charge sign and to reciprocal rescaling of Q and mu, so the repair cannot select the compact generator or its normalization. It is a conditional dynamical completion after a reduction is supplied, not the reduction law itself.
